ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$ at point $D$, $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $F$, and $AC=BF$, $DF=DC$. If $\angle ABE=15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle DBF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \perp BC$, \\
therefore $\angle BDF = \angle ADC = 90^\circ$, \\
In right triangles $\triangle BDF$ and $\triangle ADC$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}AC=BF\\ DC=DF\end{array}\right.$, \\
therefore right $\triangle BDF \cong \triangle ADC$ (HL), \\
therefore $AD = BD$, \\
therefore $\angle ABD = \angle DAB = 45^\circ$, \\
since $\angle ABE = 15^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle DBF = \angle ABD - \angle ABE = 45^\circ - 15^\circ = \boxed{30^\circ}$.

In the right triangles BDF and ADC, it is known that BF=AC, DF=DC, therefore the two right triangles can be determined congruent by the equality of the hypotenuse and one right-angle side, that is, △BDF≅△ADC. Thus the corresponding sides BD=AD. Also because AD⊥BD, △ABD is an isosceles right triangle, hence ∠ABD=45°. Since BE and BF are in the same straight-line direction, ∠ABF=∠ABE=15°, and BF is inside ∠ABD, so ∠DBF=∠ABD−∠ABF=45°−15°=30°.
